SetUpARepo
A person starts a repository with farrier. They write the starter agents.yml, list the demo skill and the
    scaffold in it as the Next line asks, render the install, and seed a folder from the scaffold twice into two
    places. Running the scaffold again keeps what it wrote.

ReplaceAConfig
A person has an agents.yml they wrote by hand. init refuses to replace it. With --force it writes the starter
    in its place. They list the demo skill again and install, then force a fresh starter, which drops the
    selection, and install once more: the skill the config no longer selects is removed.

WrongTurns
A person runs farrier out of order. install with no agents.yml is told to run init. A scaffold on a repo with
    no agents.yml is offered everything the library defines. After init, a scaffold the config does not list is not
    enabled, an unknown one is refused with the ids the library defines, and a library that does not exist is
    refused before anything else is read.

ConfigureTheMachine\nA person reads the home config, which sets nothing but its version, and asks for a key it defaults. They set the default CLI, read it back from the file, and are refused a name with no equals sign, a key the config does not have and a key nothing sets. They read the reference for a key, record the worktree, stablemate and base directories, are refused a directory that holds no library, and record the library. The listing then shows every key in the order the schema gives.

ReadTheLibrary\nA person reads the library the layer stack resolves: the catalog, one skill as written, a skill the library lacks, a show with no kind named, and the check of its front matter. A library that does not exist is refused. They also ask what workflows this machine has, none, the version, and the worktrees of a folder that holds no checkout.

ReleaseAndTraceASkill\nA person installs the demo skill and asks where the generated file comes from. They are told the library file. A file farrier did not write and a file that is not there are refused. They eject the skill, which hands the folder over and drops the selection. A second eject finds nothing to hand over, and the same file now names no source.

WireTheHooks\nA person checks a repository with no agents.yml and is told to run init. After init the doctor warns that no services are declared. Hooks list says there is no library, hooks install announces its steps with --dry-run and then wires them. The commit checks and the sync print nothing. Once the library is recorded the listing shows each stage empty.

InstallForEveryRepo\nA person installs the user library before the home config has one and is refused. They add a table that names the demo skill, install again and the skill lands in the home. Installing again changes nothing.
- **bare**: the repository holds no agents.yml. Reached by: a fresh service, nothing done.
- **user-library**: the home config lists a user library and the repository holds no agents.yml. Reached by: ListUserLibrary.
- **hand-configured**: a person wrote agents.yml by hand. Reached by: HandWriteConfig.
- **initialized**: init wrote the starter agents.yml. Reached by: farrier init --repo ..
- **installed**: the starter lists the demo skill and the scaffold, and install has run. Reached by: farrier init --repo .; ListWhatIsWanted; farrier install --repo . --library lib.

elements: ConfigShow, ConfigGet, ConfigSet, ConfigSetWorktree, ConfigSetStablemate, ConfigSetLibrary, ConfigSetBase, FileRecord
The watch marks each key of the home config by its name and never by its value: `worktree_dir = "` says the key is
set. The book gives every directory key one value, the folder the sandbox holds for it (`lib`, `st`, `wt`), so the
model prints that value in `config show` and `config get` without holding it in the row. A directory that does not
exist is refused only for the library and the base, as `farrier/farrier/cli.py::_dispatch_config` checks. The value
of `default_cli` is held only when it is `codex`, the one the book sets. `config set` keeps any other value
verbatim, which the model echoes and does not hold.
`config show` lists the keys in the order of the schema, whatever order the file holds them in, with the
`[user_library.*]` table last, as a Python dictionary.

elements: Worktrees, Workflows, WorkflowNames
`farrier worktrees` walks the checkouts under the folders it is given and under the configured `worktree_dir`
(`farrier/farrier/worktree_sweep.py`). The sandbox holds no git checkout, so the listing is empty and the command
exits 0 without the "Nothing changed" line. `farrier workflows` reads the pipx environments of the machine; the
sandbox's home is a folder of its own, so no distribution is installed and the command says so. `--names` prints one
empty line in that case. A machine with workflows installed lists them, which the book does not state.

elements: Install, Scaffold
The book always sends --library and never plays it left out. Without it farrier falls back to the library of the
machine it runs on: $FARRIER_LIBRARY_DIR, the home config, then the base library it finds or ships
(farrier/farrier/layers.py:114-149). The sandbox cuts the first two and names an empty base, so the fall-back would
render no skill the book could compare. The library argument is therefore optional in the declaration, which keeps
the runtime from deriving a "missing" class for it.

elements: InstallUser
A `[user_library.codex]` table takes settings, as the Claude and Copilot tables do. Codex keeps its settings in
`~/.codex/config.toml`, the file that also holds its MCP servers and the projects the person trusted. Farrier merges
each top-level key of a library settings file into that TOML and leaves every other key, table and comment in place.
A library settings file stays JSON for every harness, so one loader reads them all. A key that holds an object, such
as `features`, becomes a TOML table, and farrier owns that table whole. A person who adds a key of their own under it
sees the next install stop with the conflict, as it does for a nested object in Claude's settings.
OpenCode still takes no settings, because its config is the JSONC file farrier only reads.

elements: InstallUser
A `[user_library.copilot]` table takes rules, MCP servers, guards, helper agents and settings, the same keys a
`[user_library.claude]` table takes. Before this, farrier wrote only skills into `~/.copilot` and refused every other
key, so a person who moved from Claude to Copilot lost the home setup the library keeps for them. Every harness farrier
knows now has a writer for each of those keys, so the refusals that named an unsupported harness are gone.
Copilot reads its home rules from `~/.copilot/copilot-instructions.md`, its servers from `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json`,
its agents from `~/.copilot/agents/*.agent.md` and its settings from `~/.copilot/settings.json`. Copilot documents that
settings file as JSONC. Farrier merges it as plain JSON, so a comment the person adds there stops the install with a
parse error. The library's Copilot settings carry no comment, and a person who wants one moves the key elsewhere.
A guard is written for Claude's hook input. Copilot hands a `preToolUse` hook other tool names and other fields, so
farrier writes `~/.copilot/hooks/farrier-guards.py`, a bridge that turns Copilot's input into Claude's, runs the guard,
and turns its verdict back. A guard that crashes allows the call, as it does under Claude. A guard that runs when the
agent stops is written on Copilot's `agentStop` hook, which OpenCode has no counterpart for.
The hook list itself is `~/.copilot/hooks/farrier-guards.json`. JSON holds no comment, so farrier owns that file by its
name and overwrites a hand-written file of the same name. Any other file in `~/.copilot/hooks/` is the person's.
A helper agent that names delegates gets Copilot's `agent` tool, which Copilot does not limit to named agents. The
agent's prompt names whom it hands work to, and Copilot may still let it reach another agent.

elements: Doctor
`farrier doctor` names the repository as typed, not resolved: `--repo .` reports "no agents.yml in .", and a call with
no `--repo` reports the working directory (`farrier/farrier/doctor.py::diagnose`). It reports an error and exits 1 only
when there is no agents.yml. Every config the book writes lacks a `services:` block, so the report is the one warning
and exit 0.

elements: HooksInstall, HooksList, Checks, Sync
farrier ships its base library, so every command resolves one. The sandbox names an empty base with
`STABLEMATE_BASE_DIR`, which outranks the shipped one. That keeps the answers of `hooks install`, `hooks list`,
`checks` and `sync` free of the base's content, which changes with every release. With the empty base,
`hooks install` writes `.agents/hooks/*` with no hook in them and `hooks list` reads `(none)` at every stage.
`checks` lists the repository's own `sync` check, which starts with the absolute path of the farrier that is running,
so the declaration leaves it opaque and the claim is the exit code.
`sync` is a commit check, and a commit check only runs inside a checkout. The sandbox is no git checkout, so `sync`
skips the check there and exits 0, the same answer it gives when no library resolves. It used to end in a traceback
there instead: see DISAGREEMENTS 4.

elements: Init
init ends by printing a proposed [user_library.claude] table whenever the shared config holds none and stdin is
not a terminal (farrier/farrier/cli.py:179-197). The sandbox config holds only config_version and the command
runs with stdin closed, so every run prints the proposal naming <sandbox>/config.toml. When the config holds a
[user_library.*] table the proposal is left out, and the `user-library` scene plays that case.

elements: Install
The number install prints is four launcher files, one skill file for each selected skill, and the root Makefile
only when the repository has none. The renderer adds the Makefile to its outputs when the path does not exist
(farrier/farrier/renderer.py:769-771) and the count is the size of that map (farrier/farrier/cli.py:289). A
second install of the same repository therefore prints one fewer than the first. Where the repository already has
a Makefile, install appends the include block to it and prints a line about that (farrier/farrier/outputs.py:707).

elements: InstallUser, ListUserLibrary
`farrier install --user` renders what the `[user_library.<harness>]` tables of the home config select into the
harness homes, and refuses when the config has none (`farrier/farrier/user_library.py::user_library_tables`,
`farrier/farrier/cli.py::_run_user_install`). `farrier init` only proposes the table, so a person writes it by hand,
and the book names that act an outside event. The table the book writes selects the demo skill, which the library
renders to `<home>/.claude/skills/demo/SKILL.md` with the same generated-by marks as a repository install. A home
other than the one the sandbox holds writes where the watch does not look, so the model changes no watched file for it.

elements: Scaffold, enabled, not_enabled
A repository with no agents.yml may apply any scaffold the library defines, and one with an agents.yml may apply
only the scaffolds it lists (farrier/farrier/scaffolds.py:160-167). The model reads that off the watched
agents.yml: no file, or a file that holds "- service-gitignore". The same test decides whether the listing prints
the scaffold or the "No scaffolds available" sentence (farrier/farrier/cli.py:582-583). Aimed at a directory that
does not exist, scaffold finds no agents.yml there and creates the directory with the files in it, so the
elsewhere class of the repo argument succeeds.

elements: LibraryList, LibraryShow, LibraryCheck, Source, Eject
The library commands are played with `--library lib`, the folder the sandbox seeds with one skill, `demo`, and one
scaffold. The catalog lists the demo skill with the layer it comes from and the scaffold under its own kind, and
`library check` counts one source because a scaffold definition carries no front matter. The sandbox names an empty
base library (`STABLEMATE_BASE_DIR`), which outranks the one farrier ships, so the overlay holds every source.
`farrier source` answers for a file install generated with the library file it came from, and refuses a file that
exists and carries no `metadata.source` or banner. `farrier eject` hands the generated skill folder over: it drops
`- demo` from the `skills:` list of agents.yml, leaves the folder in place without the generated marks, and renders
again, which writes five files because the skill is no longer one of them. Ejecting the same name again finds no
generated skill, and the refusal lists none.

elements: Install, Scaffold, no_library_to_install, no_library_to_scaffold
A directory is a usable library when it holds a library/ folder, and nothing else is required of it.
`is_library_dir` (farrier/farrier/_vendor/stablemate_core/layout.py:8-10)
tests only `(path / "library").is_dir()`. resolve_library_dir (farrier/farrier/layers.py:122-127) resolves the
path against the working directory and refuses a directory without library/ with the sentence the rules quote.
The book's seed library holds library/ and scaffolds/ and no packs/, so every run proves the tool does not
need packs/.

elements: Init, Install, Scaffold, FileRecord
Programs print absolute paths, and a sandbox is a new directory for every world. The surface writes the sandbox
path as <sandbox> in everything the program printed, so a message built from a path is the same text in every
world and the rules quote it. The directory is named acme because farrier prefixes the skills it installs with the
kebab-cased name of the repository's directory (farrier/farrier/naming.py, repo_prefix), so the skill lands at
.claude/skills/acme-demo.

elements: Install
farrier/farrier/_vendor/stablemate_core is a symlink to core/stablemate_core, the shared package that holds the
config, schema and manifest readers every command calls. Its files are core's, not farrier's, and the vendored
checksum beside it only records which copy farrier took. The book names the farrier files that call it and leaves the
link, its checksum and the package marker under `App(ignore=...)`. The README of the package and its `__init__.py`
hold no behaviour.

elements: Install
install prints "Updated .agents .gitignore rules" when it changes the ignore file (farrier/farrier/outputs.py:696-697),
Wired `make farrier-run-hook` into ... when it wires the hook (the hook manager lines at outputs.py:703-705) and
Added agent launcher include to root Makefile when it appends to an existing Makefile (outputs.py:706-707).
Each is printed once and not again, so the line depends on whether the repository already held the result of an
earlier run. The model keeps the files, not those histories, so the answer leaves the three lines out of the
comparison. The files they describe are still watched.

elements: Version, ConfigReference
`farrier version` prints the version of the installed distribution and `farrier config reference` prints the
documentation of the keys, which the library edits with each release. The book states neither text: both declarations
leave every line opaque, so the claim is the exit code. A key no config file has is refused with a message the book
does state (`farrier/farrier/config_reference.py::reference_text`).
